hints.title: Floor Baseline Sum
hints.text: Calculate the sum when every price is rounded down. The target must lie between the floor sum and the ceiling sum; otherwise no valid rounding exists.

hints.title: Upward Rounding Quota
hints.text: The difference between target and the floor sum determines exactly how many non-integer prices must be rounded up instead of down.

hints.title: Sort by Fractional Magnitude
hints.text: Rounding up an item with fractional part f replaces error f with 1 - f. To minimize total error, pick the k items with the largest fractional parts to round up.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
import math

class Solution:
    def minimizeError(self, prices: list[str], target: int) -> str:
        floors = []
        fracs = []
        for p in prices:
            val = float(p)
            f = math.floor(val)
            floors.append(f)
            frac = val - f
            if frac > 1e-9:
                fracs.append(frac)

        min_sum = sum(floors)
        max_sum = min_sum + len(fracs)
        if target < min_sum or target > max_sum:
            return "-1"

        k = target - min_sum
        fracs.sort(reverse=True)
        total_error = sum(1.0 - fracs[i] for i in range(k)) + sum(fracs[i] for i in range(k, len(fracs)))
        return f"{total_error:.3f}"
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all 2^N rounding configurations takes exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting fractional components enables an optimal greedy assignment in O(N log N) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that rounding up items with larger fractional parts minimizes total error.
complexity.notes: Format answer as string with exactly three decimal places.
